title: ElectronHoverLink: constrain routing to 45° bends and reduce traveling glow intensity

requirements.summary: Update ElectronHoverLink canvas path routing to avoid excessive turning and constrain bends to max 45° (HV segments with 45° diagonals only).
acceptanceCriteria: When hovering a category, the rendered connection track only uses straight horizontal/vertical segments and 45° diagonal transitions (no sharper-than-45° corners).
Compared to the current behavior, the track path shows visibly less exaggerated turning/detouring between origin and target across typical screen sizes.
The effect still renders correctly during hover and during the existing fade-out behavior (no flicker, no broken path).

file_operations.description: Refactor calculatePCBPath to generate a more direct PCB-style route with only horizontal/vertical segments connected by true 45° diagonals (equal |dx| and |dy| for diagonal legs). Clamp/guard diagonal lengths to avoid over-long detours, prefer the shortest valid route (e.g., choose whether to resolve X or Y first based on relative distances), and ensure no extra intermediate turns are introduced. Keep the existing hover + stored fade-out state behavior intact and compatible with the new path output.

requirements.summary: Reduce the intensity (perceived brightness) of the traveling glow trail and glow head while preserving style and timing.
acceptanceCriteria: The traveling glow trail appears subtly dimmer/less intense than before (lower perceived brightness), without disappearing.
The moving glow head is also slightly less intense than before while remaining clearly visible.
Static track rendering (solid + dashed) and fade-in/fade-out behavior continue to work as they do currently.

file_operations.description: Tune the traveling glow rendering parameters (trail gradient alpha and head gradient alpha/stops, and if needed the glow sizes) to be subtly dimmer while keeping the same travelDuration, glowSegmentLength behavior, and fade envelope. Ensure solid + dashed track strokes and the existing fade-in/fade-out remain unchanged in timing and stability.
